question.text: Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund has NAV INR 500 cr and gross exposure INR 950 cr (leverage 1.9x). Prime broker triggers a margin call if leverage exceeds 2.0x. A sudden drawdown causes NAV to drop. At what NAV will the fund breach 2.0x (assuming gross stays INR 950 cr)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Leverage = Gross / NAV. 2.0x breach when NAV = Gross / 2 = 950 / 2 = INR 475 cr. A NAV drop of 25 cr (5% drawdown) is enough to breach the SEBI 2x Cat III cap — tight buffer. The Trap: Option A is current NAV (no breach). Option C is 10% drawdown (deeper than trigger). Option B is 20% drawdown (way past trigger). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D doesn't apply (Cat I/II no leverage). VIII (Derivatives) tests margin-utilisation math. XIX-C covers same. Manager's Pro-Tip: Standing rule: if gross leverage crosses 1.85x EOD, auto-deleverage by 3% on lowest-conviction sleeve before next market open — this keeps you clear of both the prime broker trigger AND the SEBI cap, with one day of cushion for admin lag.
